gate: These are 0.5.0 design targets, not pass/fail limits. The CI performance gate is the matched comparison with agrep 0.4.9 (crates/agrep/examples/matched.rs) on every hosted runner, against agrep==0.4.9 installed from PyPI into an isolated environment: on the mixed 100000-row, dense 2000000-row and semantic workloads, every sample of both versions must be verified and every case needs the candidate's median and p95 strictly below 0.4.9's, over the samples its early-stop schedule takes (docs/DISTRIBUTION.md). A case 0.4.9 crashes or mis-exits is never a win; a degraded 0.4.9 answer (expected exit, unprovable result) is a lower bound the candidate must beat at median and p95 with every sample verified. The bench and bench/semantic_owner.py print measured-vs-target lines and fail only on missing or wrong results.

runner_classes.ubuntu-24.04: Design targets on hosted x64 Linux, without host-specific slack; the matched gate runs on this runner.
runner_classes.ubuntu-24.04-arm: Same targets on hosted arm64 Linux; architecture is not grounds for widening them.
runner_classes.macos-15: M-series reference class; the targets apply directly.
runner_classes.macos-15-intel: Same targets on hosted x64 macOS; architecture is not grounds for widening them.
runner_classes.windows-latest: Same targets on hosted x64 Windows, including process startup.
runner_classes.windows-11-arm: Same targets on hosted arm64 Windows, including process startup.

reasons.latency_scope: Every latency target below is the design number, applied unscaled on every synthetic workload: per-call cost is dominated by process start, database open and bounded top-k work rather than corpus size, so a smaller corpus gets no smaller target, and meeting it on a small corpus is not evidence for a full history, which is measured separately on a real one. Dense-workload targets carry 2x headroom for 2M-row workloads on hosted runners: a factor of 0.5 on the ordinary target, for median and p95; first_index uses dense_index_ms and the written size factor. Warm cases report median and p95 against their target; first-index cases report every sample.
reasons.keyword_p50_ms: Warm keyword p50 <=40 ms; all search shapes, including counts and compact rendering, finish the full process.
reasons.keyword_p95_ms: Warm keyword p95 <=80 ms; 20 samples minimum, none discarded.
reasons.recall_ms: recall <=250 ms warm; pack shares this target.
reasons.census_ms: No-change census <=15 ms, measured through the full stat-census command exit.
reasons.incremental_ms: One-session incremental refresh <=50 ms through full index command exit.
reasons.first_index_ms: First full index of a large real history (reference_rows visible rows, reference_text_bytes of indexed text) <=60 s. A synthetic workload gets 60000 x min(1, max(rows / reference_rows, text_bytes / reference_text_bytes)): with build cost linear in rows and indexed text, that is the longest an engine meeting the full-history target could take on it. Example: 100000 rows with 88600000 text bytes gives 60000 x 0.1 = 6000 ms. The 1000-row semantic workload has no build target: fixed per-build costs dominate at that size, and builds are measured by the mixed and dense workloads.
reasons.dense_index_ms: The first_index_ms derivation with 2x headroom for 2M-row workloads: 30000 x the same factor, which is 1 because 2M rows exceed reference_rows.
reasons.dense_p50_ms: 2x headroom for 2M-row workloads: half the 40 ms keyword p50 target.
reasons.dense_p95_ms: 2x headroom for 2M-row workloads: half the 80 ms keyword p95 target.
reasons.hybrid_p50_ms: Warm agent hybrid p50 <=200 ms, with a labeled semantic row required. The CI semantic workload holds 1000 vectors, so this target covers model load, query embedding, keyword retrieval, fusion and rendering; vector-scan cost at large scale is measured on the 200000-reference semantic workload.
reasons.hybrid_first_ms: First hybrid query with the model installed <=1 s: a fresh CLI process after model installation and corpus embedding, with meaning results required.
reasons.reference_rows: Visible rows in the maintainer's full-history build: 130469 prose + 1071908 tool rows.
reasons.reference_text_bytes: Indexed text in the maintainer's history: about 820 MB of tool text plus 66 MB of prose.
reasons.semantic_cpu_rows_s: Bulk CPU embedding floor for 200-token rows with the full 1024-token input window retained.
reasons.semantic_metal_rows_s: Bulk Metal embedding floor for 200-token rows, without a shorter embedding window.
reasons.semantic_owner_p50_ms: Fresh-process semantic-only p50 at 200000 vector references, including normal freshness and process exit. A smaller vector fixture cannot meet this target.
reasons.hybrid_owner_p50_ms: Fresh-process hybrid p50 at 200000 vector references, with keyword time reported separately. A smaller vector fixture cannot meet this target.
reasons.semantic_owner_p95_ms: The 120 ms semantic target applies to p95 as well as p50, with no tail slack or discarded samples.
reasons.hybrid_owner_p95_ms: The 200 ms hybrid target applies to p95 as well as p50, with no tail slack or discarded samples.
reasons.semantic_tail_outlier_multiple: Every sample whose wall latency exceeds two times its mode p50 is attributed; this is an attribution trigger, not permission to discard samples.
